knowledge:
- key_parameters: idvars=Character vector of column names in the flat data frame that uniquely identify a well globally ;; primerid=Column name specifying the feature (gene/marker) measured ;; measurement=Column name containing the log-expression measurement ;; ncells=Column name containing the number of cells or other normalizing factor for the well ;; exprs_value/exprs_values=Specifies which assay slot to use, defaulting to the first matching log-like assay name (e.g., 'thresh', 'et', 'Et', 'logcounts') ;; method=Set to 'glmer' for mixed-effects models (using lme4) or 'glm' to bypass the default Bayesian logistic regression prior ;; useContinuousBayes=Logical indicating whether to use Bayesian linear regression for the continuous component ;; doLRT=Character specifying the coefficient/contrast to test using a likelihood ratio test during summary ;; hook=Function called after each regression (e.g., combined_residuals_hook to extract residuals) ;; R=Number of bootstrap replicates for GSEA, which should be set to >50 for real analyses
- alternatives: scater/scran=Mentioned for quality control (e.g., addPerCellQC) and visualization (e.g., plotColData, runPCA). Use these for general QC and visualization, then upcast to MAST using SceToSingleCellAssay for Hurdle model testing ;; zinbwave=Mentioned for zero-inflated factor analysis. Use zinbwave to extract latent factors, then use MAST (zlm) to characterize which genes drive those factors ;; lme4/glmer=Integrated directly into MAST's zlm (via method='glmer') for mixed-effects modeling when handling random effects (e.g., multiple cells per subject)
- when_to_use: Appropriate for single-cell transcriptomics data (qPCR or RNA-seq) characterized by zero-inflation and bimodality, where one wants to model both the probability of expression (discrete component) and the level of expression given it is expressed (continuous component) using a Hurdle model.
- pitfalls: Log-transformation expectation=MAST expects log-transformed, scale-normalized data (e.g., log2(TPM + 1) or Et = Cmax - Ct). Providing raw integer counts directly to MAST's modeling functions will lead to incorrect statistical inference ;; Covariates with NA=MAST throws an uninformative error if a covariate used in zlm contains NA values ;; Bootstrap size=For GSEA, using too few bootstrap replicates (e.g., R = 4 in the vignette) is inadequate for real reporting; R > 50 is recommended ;; Big n performance=MAST's underlying linear models scale linearly or worse with the number of cells, which can cause performance issues for very large datasets even if they fit in memory

workflows.name: qpcr_fluidigm_workflow
workflows.intent: Import qPCR cycle threshold (Ct) data from a flat data frame, convert to expression thresholds, filter outliers, and perform differential expression testing using a Hurdle model.
input: qpcr_data.csv (flat data frame containing Ct values, cell metadata, and gene identifiers)
workflows.stages:
1. Compute expression threshold (Et) from cycle threshold (Ct) using computeEtFromCt.
2. Import flat data frame into a FluidigmAssay object using FromFlatDF.
3. Subset and split the assay by cell metadata.
4. Filter low-quality wells using plotSCAConcordance and mast_filter.
5. Fit a Hurdle model using zlm and perform differential expression testing using lrTest or LRT.
workflows.code:
vbeta <- computeEtFromCt(vbeta)
vbeta.fa <- FromFlatDF(vbeta, idvars=c("Subject.ID", "Chip.Number", "Well"),
                          primerid='Gene', measurement='Et', ncells='Number.of.Cells',
                          geneid="Gene",  cellvars=c('Number.of.Cells', 'Population'),
                          phenovars=c('Stim.Condition','Time'), id='vbeta all', class='FluidigmAssay')
sub1 <- vbeta.fa[,1:10]
sub2 <- subset(vbeta.fa, Well=='A01')
sub3 <- vbeta.fa[6:10, 1:10]
sp1 <- split(vbeta.fa, 'Subject.ID')
cbind(sp1[[1]],sp1[[2]])
vbeta.split<-split(vbeta.fa,"Number.of.Cells")
plotSCAConcordance(vbeta.split[[1]],vbeta.split[[2]],
                   filterCriteria=list(nOutlier = 1, sigmaContinuous = 9,
                       sigmaProportion = 9))
vbeta.filtered <- mast_filter(vbeta.fa, groups='ncells')
was.filtered <- mast_filter(vbeta.fa, apply_filter=FALSE)
head(subset(was.filtered, pctout))
burdenOfFiltering(vbeta.fa, 'ncells', byGroup=TRUE)
vbeta.1 <- subset(vbeta.fa, ncells==1)
vbeta.1 <- vbeta.1[1:20,]
zlm.output <- zlm(~ Population + Subject.ID, vbeta.1,)
coefAndCI <- summary(zlm.output, logFC=FALSE)$datatable
zlm.lr <- lrTest(zlm.output, 'Population')
two.sample <- LRT(vbeta.1, 'Population', referent='CD154+VbetaResponsive')

workflows.name: scrnaseq_hurdle_analysis
workflows.intent: Import single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix and metadata, perform adaptive thresholding, calculate cellular detection rate, fit a Hurdle model, and extract model residuals.
input: expression_matrix.csv (genes x cells matrix of log-transformed expression values)
workflows.stages:
1. Import expression matrix and metadata into a SingleCellAssay using FromMatrix.
2. Filter cells and genes based on quality metrics and expression frequency.
3. Recalculate cellular detection rate (CDR) and add to cell metadata.
4. Apply adaptive thresholding using thresholdSCRNACountMatrix.
5. Fit Hurdle model adjusting for CDR and condition using zlm.
6. Summarize differential expression and perform likelihood ratio tests.
7. Extract model residuals using combined_residuals_hook.
workflows.code:
scaRaw <- FromMatrix(t(maits$expressionmat), maits$cdat, maits$fdat)
filterCrit <- with(colData(scaRaw), pastFastqc=="PASS"& exonRate >0.3 & PercentToHuman>0.6 & nGeneOn> 4000)
sca <- subset(scaRaw,filterCrit)
cdr2 <-colSums(assay(sca)>0)
colData(sca)$cngeneson <- scale(cdr2)
thres <- thresholdSCRNACountMatrix(assay(sca), nbins = 20, min_per_bin = 30)
assays(sca, withDimnames = FALSE) <- list(thresh=thres$counts_threshold, tpm=assay(sca))
expressed_genes <- freq(sca) > freq_expressed
sca <- sca[expressed_genes,]
cond<-factor(colData(sca)$condition)
cond<-relevel(cond,"Unstim")
colData(sca)$condition<-cond
zlmCond <- zlm(~condition + cngeneson, sca)
summaryCond <- summary(zlmCond, doLRT='conditionStim')
summaryDt <- summaryCond$datatable
predicted <- predict(zlmCond,modelmatrix=MM)
scaDE <- sca[entrez_to_plot,]
zlmResidDE <- zlm(~condition + cngeneson, scaDE, hook=combined_residuals_hook)
residDE <- zlmResidDE@hookOut
residDEMatrix <- do.call(rbind, residDE)
assays(scaDE, withDimnames = FALSE) <- c(assays(scaDE), list(resid=residDEMatrix))

workflows.name: gene_set_enrichment_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform competitive gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on Hurdle model coefficients using bootstrapping to account for intergene correlation.
input: gene_sets.gmt (GMT file containing gene sets of interest)
workflows.stages:
1. Bootstrap the variance-covariance matrix of the fit using bootVcov1.
2. Load gene sets from a GMT file using getGmt and map to indices using limma::ids2indices.
3. Run competitive gene set enrichment analysis using gseaAfterBoot.
4. Summarize and extract significant modules.
workflows.code:
boots <- bootVcov1(zlmCond, R = 4)
module_file <- list.files(packageExt, pattern = module, full.names = TRUE)
gene_set <- getGmt(module_file)
gene_ids <- geneIds(gene_set)
sets_indices <- limma::ids2indices(gene_ids, mcols(sca)$symbolid)
sets_indices <- sets_indices[sapply(sets_indices, length) >= min_gene_in_module]
gsea <- gseaAfterBoot(zlmCond, boots, sets_indices, CoefficientHypothesis("conditionStim"))
z_stat_comb <- summary(gsea, testType='normal')
